content: 1. S. J. N., Meintjes G., Williams A., Brown Y., Crede T., and Harrison T. S. conducted a study on adult meningitis in a population with high prevalence of HIV and tuberculosis, analyzing findings from 4,961 suspected cases. This was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2010 (Volume 10, Article 67). 2. Sathyanarayanan V., Razak A., and Chakraborty J. presented a case series detailing the clinical profile of disseminated cryptococcal infection. Their findings were published in Asian Pacific Tropical Medicine in 2010 (Volume 3, Pages 818–820). 3. French N., Gray K., Watera C., Nakiyingi J., Lugada E., Moore M., and colleagues studied cryptococcal infection in a cohort of HIV-1-infected Ugandan adults. Their research appeared in AIDS in 2002 (Volume 16, Pages 1031–1038). 4. Nelson M. R., Bower M., Smith D., Reed C., Shanson D., and Gazzard B. evaluated the diagnostic utility of serum cryptococcal antigen in detecting cryptococcal infection in HIV-infected patients. This study was published in Journal of Infection in 1990 (Volume 21, Pages 175–181). 5. Jarvis J. N., Percival A., Bauman S., Pelfrey J., Meintjes G., Williams G. N., and colleagues assessed a novel point-of-care cryptococcal antigen test using serum, plasma, and urine samples from patients with HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2011 (Volume 53, Pages 1019–1023). 6. Williams D. A., Kiiza T., Kwizera R., Kigundu R., Velamakanni S., Meya D. B., and colleagues evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a fingerstick cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay in HIV-infected individuals. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2015 (Volume 61, Pages 464–467). 7. Guidelines for the diagnosis, prevention, and management of cryptococcal disease in HIV-infected adults, adolescents, and children were developed and published as a comprehensive resource. 8. Longley N., Jarvis J. N., Meintjes G., Boulle A., Cross A., Kelly N., and colleagues conducted a prospective cohort study on cryptococcal antigen screening in patients initiating antiretroviral therapy (ART) in South Africa. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016 (Volume 62, Pages 581–587). 9. Lindsley M. D., Mekha N., Baggett H. C., Surinthong Y., Autthateinchai R., Sawatwong P., and colleagues evaluated a newly developed lateral flow immunoassay for diagnosing cryptococcosis. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2011 (Volume 53, Pages 321–325). 10. Helou S., Robles A. M., Arechavala A. I., Bianchi M. H., and Negroni R. studied respiratory cryptococcosis in HIV-positive patients, with their findings published in Revista Iberoamericana de Micología in 1999 (Volume 16, Pages 126–129). 11. Taelman H., Bogaerts J., Batungwanayo J., Van de Perre P., Lucas S., and Allen S. reported on the failure of the cryptococcal serum antigen test to detect primary pulmonary cryptococcosis in HIV-infected patients. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1994 (Volume 18, Pages 119–120). 12. Boulware D. R., Rolfes M. A., Rajasingham R., von Hohenberg M., Qin Z., Taseera K., and colleagues conducted a multisite validation of the cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay and its quantification using laser thermal contrast. Their findings were published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2014 (Volume 20, Pages 45–53). 13. Binnicker M. J., Jespersen D. J., Bestrom J. E., and Rollins L. O. compared four assays for detecting cryptococcal antigen. This study was published in Clinical Vaccine Immunology in 2012 (Volume 19, Pages 1988–1990). 14. Boulware D. R., Meya D., Longley N., Govender N., Jarvis J., Neary B., and colleagues conducted a multicenter evaluation of a novel point-of-care assay for detecting cryptococcal antigen in HIV-infected individuals with and without cryptococcal meningitis. This research was presented at the 52nd Interscience Conference on Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in San Francisco, CA, from September 9–12, 2012.
